## National Forecasting and Warning Service

The National Forecasting and Warning Service (NFWS) runs flood models, data pipelines, code tools, and warning systems across multiple teams. The work is operationally consequential: outputs inform real decisions during flood events. That demands documented standards.

This book (`governance-core`) defines the standards that apply across NFWS: role definitions, the tier system for asset classification, quality thresholds, and companion standards for each asset type. It does not name individual role holders or record specific team assets. That responsibility belongs to each team.

Every in-scope team maintains its own governance repository (`governance-<team>`). That repository names the current role holders, records the team's assets, pins to a `governance-core` release, and documents any formal departures from core standards.

The two teams currently in scope are the Forecasting Team and the Warning Team. The Flood Forecasting Centre operates under separate governance arrangements and is outside this framework's scope.

## How a team adopts this framework

1. Create a `governance-<team>` repository from the starter template.
2. Pin to the current `governance-core` release in `index.qmd`.
3. Fill in named role holders in `roles.qmd`.
4. Register Tier 3 assets in `assets.qmd`.
5. Identify shared datasets and notify the central data team Steward.
6. Note the assigned central data team liaison in `index.qmd`.

## Version 3.0 Changes

This version restructures the document from a single-team book to a departmental framework covering all NFWS teams. Three new chapters have been added: Central Data Team, Shared Datasets, and Future Directions. Two new companion stubs are included: Flood Warning Asset Governance and Procedure Tools Governance. All existing companion documents have been updated to version 2.0.
:::
